book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: What does AMD do, why did it plunge 41% off its high, and why is our independent verdict REJECTED despite booming Data Center revenue?

epigraph.quote: A great company is not a great investment if you pay too much—or buy it while the foundation is cracking.
epigraph.author: Institutional Risk Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMD) designs cloud server CPUs (EPYC), AI accelerators (Instinct MI350 and MI450), PC chips (Ryzen), and adaptive FPGAs (Xilinx) [1][2]. Operating growth is surging right now. Q3 2026 revenue climbed +45% YoY to $13.38 billion [2][3]. Data Center sales jumped +97% YoY to $8.55 billion at a 33.7% operating margin, and Q4 guidance sits near $17.0 billion (+66% YoY) [2][3]. Even so, our price-blind Pass 1 audit graded AMD CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL (kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH). That growth came with a steep forensic bill: $81.8 billion in off-balance-sheet commitments, $11.46 billion in inventory (an EY Critical Audit Matter), and a November 23 Form S-3ASR registering 336.93 million resale shares (~20.5% dilution) [1][2][26].

Dual Verdict (As of November 24, 2026 — CMP $387.65): New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0) on VALUATION and TREND. AMD has dropped 41.1% from its $658.52 high into a confirmed Weinstein Stage 4 breakdown [28]. Price sits 23.38% below the $505.92 30-week SMA and 10.45% below the $432.87 200-day SMA [28]. Only 2.1% of semiconductor stocks trade above their 50-DMA inside a 10-distribution-day S&P 500 Downtrend [28]. Meanwhile, AMD trades at 84.26x TTM GAAP P/E and 21.51x headline Forward P/E (~26x diluted), more than double NVIDIA's 8.66x Forward P/E [27][33]. Our fully diluted Base fair value ($375.00) and expected value ($349.50) both sit below CMP. Current holding action is NOT_HELD (0 shares across Schwab and Robinhood), and 100% of marginal USD capital stays in cash.

Shortlist Pipeline Note: You requested adding AMD to the shortlist before underwriting. Our deterministic pipeline rules route REJECTED / TIER_0 setups to data/discarded/US.json with explicit re-entry triggers. This keeps the active shortlist focused strictly on Stage 2 setups with clear asymmetry. AMD remains on monitored radar and will promote once its four re-evaluation gates clear.
The summary table anchors every verdict to our November 24, 2026 market cutoff, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, and November 23 Form S-3ASR filing [2][26][27][28].

web_blocks.html: Across all three investment horizons, broken Stage 4 momentum and fully diluted valuation risk outweigh headline Data Center revenue growth. The chapters ahead trace AMD's ten-year history, segment economics, forensic footnotes, valuation math, and exact re-entry gates.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our institutional monograph on Advanced Micro Devices. Few companies in global technology have staged a comeback as dramatic as AMD's decade-long march under Lisa Su—from a $2 near-bankruptcy survivor to a $635 billion AI and data center powerhouse guiding to $17 billion in quarterly revenue.

Yet as you and I sit down to underwrite AMD on November 25, 2026, the market is sending a loud warning. The stock has crashed 41% from its $658.52 peak to $387.65, shedding 24% in the past week alone. Most investors see a 41% drop in a famous AI leader and immediately reach for the buy button. Our job is to resist that reflex and check the footnotes first.

That forensic discipline paid off in Pass 1. Beneath AMD's dazzling +97% Data Center growth lies an $81.8 billion tower of off-balance-sheet supplier orders, data center leases, and partner credit guarantees, alongside $11.46 billion in inventory and a fresh November 23 Form S-3ASR filing registering 336.9 million shares for potential resale. Pair that 20.5% dilution overhang with a confirmed Weinstein Stage 4 breakdown—and with NVIDIA and Broadcom trading at far lower forward multiples—and our independent verdict is clear: REJECTED on Valuation and Trend. Let us walk through the full ten-chapter story together so you see every piece of the puzzle.

Let us be completely transparent about how we reached this conclusion. In our research process, we never let a stock chart poison our view of a business, and we never let a brilliant product roadmap blind us to a broken balance sheet or a bad entry price. That is why we ran Pass 1 completely price-blind. Before we ever looked at AMD's share price or its P/E ratio, we audited ten years of audited Form 10-K filings, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q footnotes, and the November 2026 acquisition disclosures for World Labs and Taalas.

What emerged from that blind audit is a fascinating paradox. On one side of the ledger sits an engineering triumph. EPYC server processors have taken 46.2% of x86 server CPU revenue from Intel. Data Center sales nearly doubled in Q3 2026 to $8.55 billion at a 33.7% segment operating margin. Embedded is rebounding toward 40% operating margins, and management guided Q4 2026 revenue to roughly $17.0 billion—up 66% year over year. On pure silicon execution, Lisa Su has built a genuine challenger to NVIDIA's data center dominance.

On the other side of the ledger sits the forensic bill for that hyper-growth. To secure multi-gigawatt MI450 and Helios rack deployments at OpenAI and Meta, AMD handed out 320 million penny-priced warrant shares and took on $81.8 billion in off-balance-sheet obligations: $48.76 billion in supplier purchase commitments, $13.3 billion in uncommenced data center leases, $8.5 billion in partner credit guarantees, $6.18 billion in cloud compute backstops, and $5.1 billion in private AI equity commitments. Inventory jumped 44.7% in nine months to $11.46 billion, earning a Critical Audit Matter flag from Ernst & Young. And on November 23, 2026, AMD filed Form S-3ASR registering 336.93 million shares for resale—roughly 20.5% of its entire share count.

When we unlocked the market tape in Pass 2, the verdict snapped into sharp focus. At $387.65, AMD is trading in a confirmed Weinstein Stage 4 breakdown, 23.4% below its 30-week moving average and 10.5% below its 200-day moving average. Only 2.1% of semiconductor stocks sit above their 50-day average, while the S&P 500 is trapped in a ten-distribution-day Downtrend with the 10-Year Treasury yield at 4.92%. Even after a 41% plunge, AMD's fully diluted Base fair value sits at $375.00—below today's price—while NVIDIA trades at 8.66x forward earnings with 75% gross margins. Our independent dual verdict is REJECTED for new capital and NOT_HELD (0 shares) for your portfolio, keeping 100% of marginal cash safe in USD reserves.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why We Separate Great Engineering from Great Entries
book_callouts.text: AMD's engineers deserve applause for breaking Intel's monopoly and challenging NVIDIA in AI racks. But your capital deserves a margin of safety—and buying a Stage 4 breakdown ahead of a 336.9M-share resale shelf is not a margin of safety.
